points.description: States the situation: the natural ground slope (of the region/terrain) is steeper/greater than the slope (bed slope) provided for the canal.
points.partial_credit: Half: says only that ground is steep or sloping, or mentions slope difference vaguely without comparing ground slope to canal slope.

points.description: Links this to the canal: a fall is provided so that the canal can maintain its designed (permissible) bed slope / avoid excess slope causing erosion, by dropping the water level at that point.
points.partial_credit: Half: only mentions dropping/lowering of water level without relating to the canal slope.

rubric.notes: Full marks: student says a fall is needed when the natural ground slope is greater than the canal's designed bed slope (synonyms like 'steeper terrain than canal gradient' accepted). Part marks: vague statements such as 'on sloping/steep ground' or 'to lower the water level' without the comparison. No marks for wrong conditions, e.g. ground slope less than canal slope or unrelated reasons.
